items.title: Represent the frozen review-inventory epoch and its receipt as signed gate-consumed process facts
items.context: Create one deep owner for epochId, cutoff hashes, scope digest, required lanes, wave identities, host and prompt identities, terminal states, verified finding-set digest, coverage or read evidence, saturation result, state OPEN FINALIZED INVALIDATED CANCELLED, and bounded-budget adjudication. Expose supported start and status operations. Status must return epochId, frozen cutoff, state, required lanes, current wave, per-lane progress or terminal state, verified/new finding counts, blockers and one exact next command. Do not reuse audit-only signatureTag as gate authority without a new validated canonical duplicate or finding-family disposition contract. The receipt proves inventory saturation on the frozen candidate, not correctness of later remediation.
items.userSees: After start, the terminal includes the exact fields "Review inventory epoch: <id>", "State: OPEN", "Frozen cutoff: <hash>" and "Next: lattice review_inventory_status --storyId=<id>"; status prints one row per required lane and exactly one "Next:" command.

happy.desc: Starting inventory on a REVIEW candidate creates exactly one unique epoch bound to the current story, review round, headHash, materialHash, storyFilesHash, scope digest, required lanes, wave identity, host identity and prompt identity; the returned signed artifact verifies through the canonical gate verifier.

Inventory status for an OPEN epoch deterministically shows epochId, frozen cutoff hashes, state, required lanes, current wave, every lane progress or terminal state, verified and newly verified finding counts, blocker codes, and exactly one executable next command.

After complete clean saturation, finalization emits a signed ReviewInventoryReceipt whose finding-set and coverage digests match the recorded epoch and which the transition gate recognizes only as inventory-completeness authority, never as approval of remediated code or authorization for TEST.

edge.desc: Begin or finalize fails closed with an actionable blocker when cutoff identity, scope digest, required lane set, host or prompt identity, coverage evidence, wave terminal state, or bounded-budget adjudication is missing or internally inconsistent.

Repeated begin and status calls across process reloads preserve one authoritative epoch and stable identities without creating duplicate OPEN epochs or changing the frozen cutoff; terminal FINALIZED, INVALIDATED and CANCELLED projections remain distinguishable.

Explicit cancellation records an auditable CANCELLED terminal state, retains incomplete verdicts only as advisory history, cannot be finalized later, and status provides the exact command to begin a fresh epoch.

adversarial.desc: Tampering with any signature, story or round binding, cutoff hash, scope digest, lane or wave identity, host or prompt identity, finding-set digest, or coverage digest causes canonical verification and every gate consumer to reject the artifact.

A valid receipt replayed across another story, review round, epoch, material lineage, or after terminal consumption is rejected; duplicate epoch IDs, duplicate lane identities and duplicate receipt submissions cannot increase coverage or satisfy saturation.

An audit-only signatureTag, prose PASS, raw finding claim, or forged duplicate or finding-family disposition cannot be promoted into gate authority without the separately validated canonical signed contract.

items.title: Enforce the OPEN-epoch material mutation barrier at every authoritative write boundary
items.context: While an epoch is OPEN, reject edits or commits that change source, tests, verifier, workflow policy, prompt contract or other review-subject material. Prompt guidance is insufficient: handler admission, Codex or Claude mutation hooks where supported, Git or commit checks, finding and pass binding, and lifecycle transitions must consume the same epoch fact. Revalidate the cutoff before every receipt, finalization and transition. Any unmediated material drift fail-closes the epoch to INVALIDATED, makes prior verdicts advisory only, and status reports the changed lineage plus an exact recovery command: cancel and start a fresh epoch or return to DEV. Explicit cancel preserves unfinished verdicts only as advisory history.
items.userSees: A blocked change prints "OPEN_REVIEW_INVENTORY_MATERIAL_MUTATION", "Epoch: <id>", "Changed lineage: <old> -> <new>" and one "Recovery:" command; bypassed drift changes status to the exact state "INVALIDATED".

happy.desc: While an epoch is OPEN, every authoritative handler, supported Codex or Claude mutation hook, commit guard and lifecycle transition rejects a change to source, tests, verifier, workflow policy, prompt contract or other review-subject material and reports epochId, changed subject, blocker code and an exact recovery command.

Before accepting each lane receipt, pass, finding, wave completion, finalization or transition, the consumer recomputes and compares the frozen material lineage; unchanged material proceeds and remains bound to the same epoch cutoff.

Explicit cancel safely releases the material barrier, records unfinished verdicts as advisory history only, and status directs the operator to start a fresh epoch or return to DEV without allowing the cancelled epoch to authorize remediation.

edge.desc: A non-material metadata-only update classified by the canonical material registry does not spuriously invalidate the epoch, while any story-owned material or review-contract change does invalidate it; classification and lineage are visible in status.

Material drift that bypasses admission is detected at the next authoritative operation, atomically changes OPEN to INVALIDATED, rejects that operation, marks every prior verdict advisory, shows old and current lineage, and emits exactly one recovery command.

Concurrent receipt and mutation attempts at the cutoff boundary cannot produce a mixed state: exactly one wins under authoritative serialization and the other is rejected or invalidates the epoch with no partially accepted gate evidence.

adversarial.desc: Direct filesystem edits, alternate write handlers, git commit paths, generated-file changes and unsupported hook bypasses cannot yield a valid current receipt; revalidation catches resulting material drift even when the preventative hook did not run.

A time-of-check/time-of-use mutation inserted after a successful precheck but before receipt persistence or transition consumption is rejected through an atomic or second lineage check and cannot leave a gate-valid stale artifact.

Forged old-cutoff passes, findings, duplicate dispositions or a manually restored hash cannot revive INVALIDATED or CANCELLED state, suppress the drift record, or authorize finalization or remediation DEV.

items.title: Require complete discovery lenses and a verified zero-new-finding saturation wave before inventory finalization
items.context: Run all scope and risk selected required lanes on the same cutoff, then run the completeness critic over the verified finding set. A wave is clean only when every required lane has a valid terminal receipt, mechanical coverage or bounded read evidence is complete, raw findings and duplicate claims are independently verified, and the wave adds zero new verified findings. Status exposes current wave, lane progress, new verified findings, remaining blockers and next dispatch or finalize command. Repeating the same reviewer, missing output, timeout, cancellation, unsupported host or prose-only PASS cannot satisfy saturation. New findings reopen another bounded wave on the same material; exhaustion visibly requires replan, decomposition, root-cause escalation or human adjudication and provides the corresponding command, never PASS.

happy.desc: On one unchanged cutoff, every scope/risk-selected required lane completes with a valid signed terminal receipt, mechanical coverage or bounded read evidence is complete, the completeness critic evaluates the verified finding set, and a zero-new-verified-finding wave alone permits finalization.

When a wave adds one or more independently verified findings, the immutable aggregate finding-set digest grows, finalization remains blocked, and status provides the exact next-wave dispatch command while keeping all waves on the same material cutoff.

At every step, status exposes current wave and bounded budget, per-lane progress or terminal outcome, coverage/read-evidence completeness, raw versus verified and newly verified counts, critic state, blocker codes and the single actionable dispatch or finalize command.

edge.desc: Missing output, timeout, cancellation, unsupported host, unavailable reviewer or prose-only PASS remains a visible nonterminal blocker and cannot count as lane coverage, clean saturation or permission to finalize.

Semantically duplicate raw findings are counted only after an independent canonical finding-family disposition verifies identity and evidence; an unresolved duplicate neither inflates the new count nor disappears from blockers.

If the configured wave budget is reached with new verified findings or incomplete lanes/critic, status enters a bounded-exhaustion blocker and offers replan, decomposition, root-cause escalation or human adjudication; no receipt or PASS is emitted.

adversarial.desc: Repeating the same reviewer, host identity, prompt identity, lane receipt or wave result under a different label cannot satisfy a missing required lane, two-host assurance or the zero-new saturation requirement.

A forged duplicate disposition, suppressed raw finding, omitted required file or evidence segment, missing critic, or fabricated coverage/read claim causes finalization to fail closed under canonical validation.

Changing severity, marking verified findings advisory, exhausting retries, or manually setting a clean counter cannot manufacture a zero-new wave or bypass required-lane, evidence and critic predicates.

items.title: Gate remediation DEV and subsequent final review on fresh inventory and material lineage
items.context: A valid ReviewInventoryReceipt may authorize one REVIEW to remediation-DEV transition carrying the immutable aggregated finding set; rejection reports the stale or missing fact and exact corrective command. It must not authorize TEST or certify the defective cutoff. The remediation commit creates new material and makes the inventory receipt historical; returning to REVIEW must compute and display impacted required lanes from the repair and dependency closure, require current evidence on the repaired material, and preserve full review escalation when scope or policy cannot be proven narrow. Replace the current Round 2 plus one-receipt shortcut wherever it could be used to claim sufficient final review. Cancel and replan remain explicit, auditable operations.
items.userSees: The accepted rollback prints "Remediation authorized once by epoch <id>", the aggregate finding count/digest, and "This receipt does not authorize TEST"; final review prints "Impacted required lanes:" followed by the exact lanes and corrective command on rejection.

happy.desc: A fresh FINALIZED ReviewInventoryReceipt authorizes exactly one REVIEW-to-remediation-DEV transition carrying the immutable complete verified finding set; the transition output identifies epoch, lineage and findings and explicitly states that the defective cutoff is not certified for TEST.

After remediation creates new material, the inventory receipt becomes historical, dependency closure computes and displays impacted required final-review lanes, and every such lane supplies current signed evidence on the repaired head before REVIEW can pass.

When remediation introduces no regression, one fresh final-review epoch with all impacted lane, host and escalation requirements satisfied can advance normally; each rejected transition reports a stable blocker and exact corrective command.

edge.desc: A provably narrow repair uses the canonical dependency closure to select impacted lanes without reducing required host assurance; if scope, policy impact or closure is unknown, the system fails closed to the full required lane set.

Missing, stale, INVALIDATED, CANCELLED, wrong-round, wrong-story, wrong-lineage or already-consumed inventory receipts reject remediation DEV and show whether to finalize, begin a fresh inventory epoch, replan or return to REVIEW.

Explicit cancel or replan remains auditable, cannot be confused with remediation authorization, preserves prior evidence as historical only, and leaves lifecycle state with exactly one valid next action.

adversarial.desc: Replaying one valid inventory receipt for a second DEV transition, using it to enter TEST directly, or treating its defective-cutoff saturation as implementation approval is rejected at every transition consumer.
The historical round-2-plus single-receipt condition cannot claim sufficient final review when any impacted lane, required host, escalation verdict or repaired-material binding is absent or stale.

A post-remediation regression or scope expansion found by any final-review lane reopens the appropriate finding and remediation flow, invalidates clean-final-review claims, and cannot be hidden by old passes, narrow-closure claims or the inventory receipt.

items.title: Prove the epoch reduces review churn without weakening escaped-defect assurance
items.context: Replay the deterministic B-cdf6 RR-043 through RR-046 failure shape, whose baseline accepted a material commit after the first lane and forced at least five later reviewer redispatches RR-047 through RR-051. Acceptance requires exactly one frozen discovery epoch before remediation, zero accepted material commits while OPEN, zero stale old-cutoff passes accepted, one aggregated remediation-DEV transition, and at most one final-review epoch when the injected remediation introduces no regression; redispatches caused by first-finding mutation must fall from at least five to zero. Required lane and host counts must not decrease, all historical critical/high cases must still be caught, and escaped critical/high findings, historical mutation survival, post-cert source commits, stale acceptance or budget-manufactured PASS must remain zero. items.title: Implement canonical post-remediation impact closure and repair the broken evidence provenance link
items.context: The current remediation made every later review round require all active lanes and removed the old targeted guidance. That preserves assurance but violates CHK-004 H2/E1 and the Story time-saving promise. Compute impacted final-review lanes from repaired material and canonical dependency closure, fail closed to all required lanes when closure, scope, or policy impact is unknown, never reduce required host assurance, and expose selected lanes and reason in operator status. Replace the decision document link to an excluded untracked B-cdf6 analysis file with tracked authoritative RR, Finding, and commit provenance.
